study.title: Visual Outcomes and Patient-Reported Symptoms after Bilateral Implantation of an Extended Depth of Focus or a Full Range of Vision Intraocular Lens
study.short_title: Bilateral PureSee or Odyssey Visual Outcomes and Symptoms
study.background:
The TECNIS PureSee is a non-diffractive extended depth of focus (EDOF) intraocular lens. Its design may reduce dysphotopsias and improve contrast sensitivity compared with diffractive lenses. A randomized controlled trial suggested better intermediate and near vision than a monofocal control, with similar contrast sensitivity, distance vision, and dysphotopsia profiles.1
The TECNIS Odyssey is a full range of vision intraocular lens. Current reports suggest high visual acuity and spectacle independence at distance, intermediate, and near.2,3
These reports concern the individual lens technologies. They do not establish which lens will provide better outcomes in the population proposed here. We would like to characterize vision and patient-reported symptoms in two cohorts followed using the same assessment schedule.
1. Corbett D, Black D, Roberts TV, Cronin B, Gunn D, Bala C, Versace P, Tsai L, Papadatou E, Alarcon A, Vilupuru S. Quality of vision clinical outcomes for a new fully-refractive extended depth of focus Intraocular Lens. Eye. 2024;38(S1):9-14. doi:10.1038/s41433-024-03039-8
2. Hacopian AG, Brunson PB, Hall B. Patient Reported Outcomes and Visual Acuity After Bilateral Implantation of a Next Generation Presbyopia Correcting Intraocular Lens. OPTH. 2026;20:1-8. doi:10.2147/OPTH.S572703
3. Bissen-Miyajima H, Midorikawa M, Fujisaki R, Ota Y, Minami K, Honda R. Early Clinical Results of a Newly Developed Continuous Range of Vision Intraocular Lens. Ophthalmol Ther. 2025;14(11):2937-2945. doi:10.1007/s40123-025-01235-7
study.hypothesis: Bilateral implantation of PureSee or Odyssey intraocular lenses will be associated with good distance and intermediate visual outcomes and high patient satisfaction. Near vision, spectacle use, and reports of visual disturbances may differ between the two cohorts. This observational study is intended to describe those outcomes; it is not designed to establish superiority of either lens.
study.timeline: Enrollment: 8 months; follow-up: 6 months after second-eye surgery; data analysis: 2 months.
study.completion: Study data analysis will begin after scheduled follow-up and database checks are complete.

population.study_population: Adults aged 50 years or older undergoing surgery for age-related cataracts in both eyes, with planned bilateral TECNIS PureSee or bilateral TECNIS Odyssey implantation selected during routine care before enrollment.
population.sample_justification: 30 evaluable subjects per cohort are estimated sufficient for descriptive characterization of visual outcomes and patient-reported symptoms. Enrollment increases to 36 per cohort (72 total) to account for dropout or incomplete 6-month assessments. No formal power calculation for superiority testing is proposed.
inclusion_criteria: Adults aged 50 years or older undergoing surgery for age-related cataracts in both eyes.
Planned bilateral implantation of either TECNIS PureSee or TECNIS Odyssey selected during routine clinical care before enrollment.
Willing and able to attend the scheduled study assessments.
No participation in another study during the 60 days before screening.
exclusion_criteria: Moderate-to-severe ocular disease deemed by the surgeon to increase the risk of complicated cataract surgery or prevent reliable visual-acuity testing.
Pseudoexfoliation syndrome with clinically significant zonular weakness, zonular dehiscence, prior ocular trauma affecting vision, or prior corneal refractive surgery.
Planned implantation of different lens models in the two eyes.

design.study_design: Prospective, observational, single-center, two-cohort study with no randomization and no masking. Cohorts are defined by lens selection already made in routine care: bilateral TECNIS PureSee or bilateral TECNIS Odyssey.
design.intervention_name: Bilateral TECNIS PureSee intraocular lenses or bilateral TECNIS Odyssey intraocular lenses, according to the preexisting routine-care treatment plan.
design.intervention_description: Lens selection will already have been made by the treating surgeon and patient as part of routine care before study enrollment. Enrollment will not determine lens selection. There will be no randomization, no masking, and no change to the planned clinical treatment. Each subject will receive the same lens model in both eyes. This study does not involve mix-and-match implantation.

arms.description: Observational cohort; 36 subjects with bilateral TECNIS PureSee implantation selected in routine care.
arms.name: Bilateral TECNIS PureSee

arms.description: Observational comparison cohort; 36 subjects with bilateral TECNIS Odyssey implantation selected in routine care. No monofocal control cohort is planned.
arms.name: Bilateral TECNIS Odyssey

design.methods_to_minimize_bias: The same eligibility criteria, visual testing conditions, testing distances, and assessment schedule will be used for both cohorts. Outcomes and analysis methods will be defined before reviewing study results. Because lens selection is not randomized and the study is not masked, differences between cohorts may reflect patient selection and other factors; a descriptive difference must not be interpreted as proof that the lens caused it.

primary: Describe and compare binocular visual outcomes, spectacle use, satisfaction, and visual disturbances after bilateral PureSee or bilateral Odyssey implantation through 6 months after second-eye surgery.

statistics.analysis_plan: All enrolled subjects will be included in descriptive enrollment and safety summaries. Visual-acuity and defocus-curve outcomes will be summarized by cohort and scheduled visit using the number of evaluable observations, mean, standard deviation, median, minimum, and maximum. AIOLIS responses will be summarized by question, response category, cohort, and scheduled questionnaire visit using counts and percentages. Available observations will be analyzed; missing observations will not be imputed. The number of participants with missing data will be reported by cohort and scheduled assessment. A participant with data at an earlier visit but no Month 6 assessment may contribute to summaries of the earlier visit, but will not contribute to the Month 6 primary-endpoint summary. Adverse events and device deficiencies will be summarized by cohort, event category, seriousness, severity, relationship, action taken, and outcome. Cohort comparisons are descriptive. No inferential hypothesis test or claim of comparative superiority is planned.

safety.monitoring: Adverse events and device deficiencies will be collected from consent through the final study contact. Scheduled review at Months 1, 3, and 6 is not the only time an event may be reported.

risks_benefits.compensation_or_reimbursement: No payment will be provided for participation. Documented travel expenses will be reimbursed up to $25 for each completed Month 1, Month 3, and Month 6 study visit, up to $75 total per participant. Screening and operative visits are not eligible for this reimbursement. A participant who withdraws may still receive reimbursement for eligible visits already completed.
risks_benefits.costs: The sponsor will pay for additional vision tests and questionnaires performed solely for this research. Routine cataract surgery, the selected lenses, and ordinary clinical care will be billed as usual to the participant or insurer. No amount of insurance coverage or participant out-of-pocket cost is specified.

paragraphs.text: Written informed consent will be obtained at preoperative screening before any study-specific prospective procedure. The consent discussion and signed form will be documented in the study records.

Study visits comprise preoperative screening, an operative visit for each eye, and postoperative assessments at Month 1, Month 3, and Month 6 (Exit). Every postoperative time point is measured from second-eye surgery. The interval between the two operations follows routine clinical care, with no fixed study interval.

items: Screening, preoperatively: obtain informed consent, collect demographics and general information including medical history, and confirm the routine-care lens selection and cohort.
Operative visit, each eye: perform cataract surgery and implant the planned lens model.

Month 1, one month after second-eye surgery: measure binocular uncorrected and corrected photopic distance visual acuity and binocular uncorrected photopic intermediate visual acuity at 66 cm; monitor for adverse events and device deficiencies.

Month 3, three months after second-eye surgery: assess binocular uncorrected and corrected photopic distance visual acuity, binocular uncorrected photopic intermediate visual acuity at 66 cm, and binocular uncorrected and distance-corrected photopic near visual acuity at 40 cm. Administer the AIOLIS questionnaire and monitor for adverse events and device deficiencies.

Month 6 (Exit), six months after second-eye surgery: obtain binocular uncorrected and corrected photopic distance visual acuity, binocular uncorrected and distance-corrected photopic intermediate visual acuity at 66 cm, and binocular uncorrected and distance-corrected photopic near visual acuity at 40 cm. Obtain the distance-corrected defocus curve, administer the AIOLIS questionnaire, monitor for adverse events and device deficiencies, and complete the exit form.

paragraphs.text: Visual acuity measurements are binocular. Distance acuity is measured both without correction and with correction at 1, 3, and 6 months after second-eye surgery. Intermediate testing uses a distance of 66 cm: uncorrected acuity is measured at those same time points, and distance-corrected acuity is measured at 6 months to provide the primary outcome, mean DCIVA for each cohort. Near testing is performed at 40 cm, without correction and with distance correction, at 3 and 6 months.

At 6 months after second-eye surgery, the binocular distance-corrected defocus curve is obtained over the range from +1.0 D through -2.50 D. Patient-reported symptoms are assessed with the Assessment of IntraOcular Lens Implant Symptoms (AIOLIS) questionnaire at 3 and 6 months. Responses are recorded for each question to support cohort-specific response percentages.
An unscheduled visit may occur when an additional study-related assessment is needed. The reason for the visit, assessments performed, and resulting actions will be documented in the study records.

A participant may stop taking part at any time. Information collected before withdrawal may remain in the study records and may be included in the analysis as permitted by the consent and applicable requirements.
The Schedule of Assessments presents the study activities and their timing, from preoperative screening through the Month 6 exit assessment.

The participant pathway includes preoperative screening, an operative visit for each eye, and Month 1, Month 3, and Month 6 (Exit) follow-up measured from second-eye surgery. The operative interval is determined by routine clinical care rather than a fixed study interval. A participant completes study follow-up after the 6-month assessment and completion of the exit form; the detailed assessment schedule is provided in Section 15.
Participants may withdraw voluntarily at any time. Withdrawal is a discontinuation disposition, not successful completion, and closeout documentation does not change that distinction.

A participant may discontinue participation at any time without penalty or loss of benefits to which the participant is otherwise entitled. The study team may document the reason when the participant chooses to provide one, and information collected before withdrawal may continue to be used as permitted by the consent and applicable requirements.
The study timeline provides for 8 months of enrollment, follow-up through 6 months after second-eye surgery, and 2 months of data analysis.
